summary: the memory suite's cases on i686, against a memory report that overstates the usable memory, a frame allocation never failed on purpose, a recovery kernel that does not refuse a machine too small, and a string sweep that finds a routine wrong

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 rach2-recovery && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: usable-overstated
faults.summary: the memory report giving 4 KiB more usable memory than the map has, which the size cases find against the map and against QEMU's size

faults.name: framefail-never
faults.summary: rach2.framefail logging the allocation it was armed to fail and then letting it succeed, which the framefail cases find

edits.find:
klog(KLOG_WARN, "vm", "frame allocation failed on purpose (rach2.framefail)");
    return 1;
edits.replace:
klog(KLOG_WARN, "vm", "frame allocation failed on purpose (rach2.framefail)");
    return 0;

faults.name: no-refusal
faults.summary: the kernel going on with less memory than it needs, which the refused case finds in the recovery kernel at 8 MiB

faults.name: strlen-wrong
faults.summary: the sweep expecting k_strlen to give 6 for hello, so that it reports the routine wrong and no sweep, which the strings case finds
